chunks: ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man from among our companions feels shy to take from zakat; so may I give him from the zakat and not tell him that it is from zakat?
So he عليه السلام said: Give it to him, and do not name it to him, and do not humiliate the believer.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: our companions, referring to fellow followers
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms being discussed as financial assistance
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer whose dignity must be protected
key_terms.لَا تُسَمِّ: do not explicitly name or identify it
key_terms.يَسْتَحْيِي: feels shy or embarrassed to accept aid

ai.seo_question: Can zakat be given to a needy believer without telling him that it is zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a believer feels ashamed to accept zakat, it may be given to him without explicitly identifying it as zakat. It combines a jurisprudential allowance with an ethical instruction to preserve the dignity of the mu'min.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1597 - Asim ibn Humayd reported from Abu Basir, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) "A man from among our companions feels embarrassed to take from Zakat. Can I give it to him without telling him that it is from Zakat?"
The Imam (as) replied: "Give it to him without mentioning that it is Zakat, and do not humiliate the believer."
